text: The three days of travel may fairly be read as a suspended sentence, in which nothing outwardly happens and everything that signifies is happening. Obedience and horror go side by side the whole way, and the narrator never suffers either to prevail over the other. Abraham's faith in this chapter is no feeling; it is a set of fixed relations, as regular as a figure in geometry. The narrator dwells on the instruments, the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire, and so names them before the act for which they were gathered.
